page.layout: One page of text, single column, with a running head at the top (Cap. 24. Jugulum Causæ.) and page number 373 at top right. Below the text: a rule, then a signature line "Aa 3" with "EPILO-" at the right (catchword-like word start), then a second rule. Pencil marks "36" in the right margin are not printed text.

main_text.p: veritatis conditio mutatur: id accedere per- notum est auditorum facilitate, qui dum ver- borum lenocinio à rerum intentionibus avocan- tur, sine delectu assentiuntur dictis omnibus; nec à rectis falsa secernunt, nescientes inesse, & in incredibili verum, & in verisimili men- dacium: certè sermo Arnaldi, ut Cecilii est siliqua sonora & eloquentiæ tumor: at Clau- dii ut Octavii rerum ipsarum soliditate li- bratus, nec tamen impar elegantiâ.

page.notes: Pencil annotation "36" in the right margin is handwriting and was omitted. The word "EPILO-" at the foot is a catchword fragment, given here as printed in the body area; the running head "Cap. 24." is part of the head and the title is set in roman/italic as printed. Some words in the italic passage are slightly blurred (e.g. "mendacium") and read with reasonable confidence.
